matrices.label: define the base style
matrices.level_1: Describe the base style by naming recognizable features of its voice in a sample piece.
matrices.level_2: Select a base style for the exercise and define it through specific voice features that can guide the draft.
matrices.level_3: Diagnose whether the chosen style can support added styles, identifying the conventions that make it recognizable and usable as a foundation for layering.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the base style into a generative premise for the piece, explaining the underlying voice logic that makes its conventions coherent and gives later styles a shared frame.

matrices.label: order the added styles
matrices.level_1: Arrange the added styles in a specified sequence after the base style, keeping the base style first.
matrices.level_2: Choose the order of the added styles to support the piece’s stated goal, placing the style that best serves that goal first.
matrices.level_3: Assess how different orders shape the transitions between styles, then sequence the additions to create a deliberate progression across the piece.
matrices.level_4: Design a sequence in which each added style changes how earlier layers are read, making the cumulative layering reshape the piece as a whole.

matrices.label: set the layer count
matrices.level_1: Identify the exercise’s specified layer count and distinguish a base style alone from a piece with added styles. Set the piece to that count.
matrices.level_2: Select a layer count that fits the exercise’s stated scope, counting the base style and each requested addition. Apply that count in the piece.
matrices.level_3: Evaluate whether the planned count gives the styles room to contribute without making the piece crowded or indistinct. Adjust the count when the layering would undermine the exercise’s aim.
matrices.level_4: Derive the layer count from the piece’s intended effect and the roles the styles need to play. Establish a flexible counting approach that adapts to different exercises rather than defaulting to two or three styles.

matrices.label: draft base style
matrices.level_1: Reproduce a short piece from a given prompt in a specified base style, using a few recognizable features of that style.
matrices.level_2: Compose a coherent short piece that applies the base style’s conventions consistently while serving the prompt.
matrices.level_3: Tailor the draft so the base style is clear and the piece provides a flexible foundation for later style layers.
matrices.level_4: Reimagine the base style’s underlying principles in an original short piece that remains recognizable and offers rich material for later layering.

matrices.label: blend second style
matrices.level_1: Add recognizable features of a second style to a short piece written in the base style, using selected words, images, or rhythms to make the added style visible.
matrices.level_2: Coordinate features of the second style across multiple parts of the piece, weaving them into the base style rather than leaving them as isolated flourishes.
matrices.level_3: Integrate the styles throughout the piece by adapting its sentences, rhythms, and structure so their conventions interact while both styles remain discernible.
matrices.level_4: Transform the interaction into a coherent hybrid mode whose overall effect depends on how the two styles reshape one another, not on either style appearing alone.

matrices.label: blend optional third style
matrices.level_1: Introduce a third style through a few identifiable choices in the piece, while keeping the base and second styles discernible.
matrices.level_2: Integrate the third style across multiple parts of the piece, coordinating its features with the existing styles rather than adding them as isolated flourishes.
matrices.level_3: Reconfigure how the three styles appear across the piece so the third style contributes to its structure and works in relation to the other layers.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the three styles into a coherent composite, transforming their familiar features into a unified stylistic effect.

matrices.label: preserve readable layering
matrices.level_1: Maintain a clear cue from the base style as a second style is added, so the short piece remains followable. Flag spots where the styles become hard to distinguish.
matrices.level_2: Arrange style cues throughout the piece so readers can follow its progression and recognize the base and added style without losing the thread.
matrices.level_3: Recalibrate the placement or strength of style cues when two or three layers compete, keeping each layer legible across the piece.
matrices.level_4: Architect a structure in which readers can trace each style through the piece while experiencing the layers as a coherent whole. Make that structure work even when the styles’ signals pull in different directions.

matrices.label: saying what each layer changed
matrices.level_1: Identify a visible change in the piece after each style layer, such as a shift in diction, rhythm, or imagery.
matrices.level_2: Compare the piece before and after each added style, attributing specific changes to that style rather than merely listing differences.
matrices.level_3: Diagnose how successive style layers modify the effects of earlier changes, distinguishing changes caused by one layer from those produced by their combination.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the changes across all layers into an account of how the piece’s overall expressive character evolves, grounding that account in specific shifts at each stage.

matrices.label: saying what it kept
matrices.level_1: Name a specific feature that remains from the base style in the layered piece, such as its diction, rhythm, or imagery.
matrices.level_2: Compare the layered piece with the base style and identify which features remain recognizable across the added style.
matrices.level_3: Trace a retained feature across two or three layers, explaining how it stays recognizable as each style shapes the piece.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the retained features across the layers into a shared formal throughline, showing what persists beneath their different stylistic expressions.

matrices.label: saying what it dropped
matrices.level_1: Identify concrete words, features, or effects that a new style layer leaves out of the piece.
matrices.level_2: Trace each omission to the layer that prompted it, and describe how the piece changes as a result.
matrices.level_3: Assess omissions across the layers, using details from the piece to distinguish deliberate removals from elements lost unintentionally.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize recurring omissions across style combinations into a transferable account of how the agent transforms source styles into a distinct writing approach.

matrices.label: noticing where two styles pull apart
matrices.level_1: Detects an obvious point in the layered piece where one style’s surface features differ from another’s, and marks the passage where the difference appears.
matrices.level_2: Compares the styles’ features within a specific passage, pinpointing how their approaches diverge there rather than merely noting a change in tone or wording.
matrices.level_3: Diagnoses whether divergences are isolated or recur across the piece, tracing a pattern of stylistic friction through the layers.
matrices.level_4: Reframes recurring points of friction as instances of a broader pattern in how the styles shape the piece, revealing a shared underlying structure beneath their apparent opposition.

matrices.label: naming what each style wants at that spot
matrices.level_1: Describe what each style appears to want at a marked point in the piece, naming a visible feature such as diction, rhythm, or image.
matrices.level_2: Differentiate the styles’ local demands by pointing to specific words or choices in the passage and stating what each style would change or preserve there.
matrices.level_3: Diagnose what each style’s demand serves in that moment, connecting its local preference to the style’s broader effect on the piece.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the styles’ demands into the larger artistic question their friction exposes, showing how each style frames that question differently without deciding which one should prevail.

matrices.label: prioritize style values
matrices.level_1: Identify which style value takes precedence at a clear point of tension in a layered piece, using a supplied priority or prompt.
matrices.level_2: Rank the competing style values at friction points in the piece, applying the ranking consistently in light of the piece’s stated aim.
matrices.level_3: Reassess the ranking across layers as the piece develops, balancing local tensions against the overall effect and taking ownership of the priorities.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize competing style values into a unifying aesthetic principle that reframes their tensions and guides priorities across the piece.

matrices.label: execute value-based choice
matrices.level_1: Apply a stated style priority at a clear point of friction, shaping the line or passage to favor that style while keeping the piece readable.
matrices.level_2: Choose which style value should lead at a specific conflict, then enact that choice in the layered piece rather than leaving the styles unresolved.
matrices.level_3: Arbitrate across several points of friction, applying a coherent priority throughout the piece while adapting individual choices to the surrounding layers.
matrices.level_4: Recast a conflict so the competing style values produce a distinct combined effect, making the piece’s resolution more than a simple win for either style.

matrices.label: explaining why one style won at the friction point
matrices.level_1: Describe a concrete feature of the friction point and give a direct reason the winning style shaped that passage. Connect the reason to an observable change in the piece.
matrices.level_2: Explain why the winning style better serves the passage’s purpose than the competing style, using a specific difference between their effects. Show how that choice shaped what the reader hears or notices.
matrices.level_3: Justify the choice by weighing what each style would contribute at the friction point and tracing the consequences of the winner across the piece. Make clear why its gains mattered more than what the other style would have preserved.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the choice into a governing principle that shows how the styles combine to create a voice neither would produce alone. Explain why the apparent winner is the best expression of that larger principle, not simply the stronger style in isolation.

matrices.label: naming what the choice shows the agent values
matrices.level_1: Identify a value directly signaled by one layering choice, such as favoring restraint or vividness, and cite the choice as evidence. State the value plainly without extending beyond that instance.
matrices.level_2: Infer the preference behind a layering choice by connecting the selected style’s influence to the agent’s stated rationale. Distinguish the underlying value from simply naming which style prevailed.
matrices.level_3: Compare choices across multiple style clashes in the piece to identify recurring or competing values. Describe the pattern while accounting for cases where the agent appears to favor different things in different moments.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize those patterns into a broader aesthetic principle that expresses what the agent values across styles. Reframe seemingly conflicting choices as instances of that principle, or identify a meaningful tension within it.
